intro: Concussion is a mild traumatic brain injury you cannot see from outside, so stay alert, give basic first aid, and escalate the emergency red flags.
points: If you ever see a red flag after a head injury, call 999 at once — a single red flag is enough.
You cannot judge concussion from the outside; there may be no cut or bruise yet still a genuine brain injury.
Symptoms can appear hours or days later, so watch the person closely for at least 24 hours.
People on blood thinners can bleed seriously from even a minor bump, so seek medical help far sooner.
Give basic first aid: encourage the person to rest, keep them calm and reassured, and stay with them.
This is awareness training, not first aid or diagnosis; your job is to recognise, respond and escalate.
